stories.title: Camber, RiseBoro Cut the Ribbon Bushwick Affordable
stories.excerpt: Camber Property Group and RiseBoro Community Partnership cut the ribbon on 1601 Dekalb Ave., which transformed a former parking lot in Brooklyn’s Bushwick neighborhood into a 127-unit, 100%t affordable residential community. The development will provide homes for some of the city’s lowest-income and most vulnerable residents alongside affordable housing for workforce households. Camber and RiseBoro co-developed the building, and RiseBoro will manage the property and provide all on-site social services to residents. The development consists of two residential towers connected by a covered walkway and centered around a shared, landscaped courtyard. “1601 Dekalb represents true mixed-income housing serving New Yorkers across a broad spectrum of income levels and we are thrilled to bring this project to Bushwick,” said Camber pirincipal Rick Gropper. “Thank you to our partners RiseBoro, HPD, HDC, Brooklyn Community Board 4 and our local electeds, for bringing this project to fruition.” The post Camber, RiseBoro Cut the Ribbon Bushwick Affordable appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Camber/RiseBoro opened 127-unit, 100% affordable project at 1601 Dekalb Ave., Bushwick.
Mixed-income serving lowest-income and workforce households with on-site social services.
Converted former parking lot; two towers connected by covered walkway and courtyard.
stories.summary: Camber Property Group and RiseBoro Community Partnership completed a 127-unit, fully affordable residential community at 1601 Dekalb Ave. in Bushwick, Brooklyn, serving both lowest-income and workforce households. The mixed-use development includes two connected towers around a shared courtyard and provides comprehensive on-site social services. RiseBoro will manage the property.
stories.impact: Confirms continued public-sector appetite for affordable development in high-opportunity Brooklyn submarkets, signaling stable capital and entitlement pathways for affordable projects. However, limited direct signal for market-rate multifamily demand or rental growth in Bushwick; primarily a policy/mission-driven deal rather than a demand indicator.

stories.title: Bank OZK Supplies $86M Construction Loan for Rental in Broward County
stories.excerpt: Bank OZK supplied a $85.5 million construction loan for Falcone Group’s multifamily development in Oakland Park, Fla. The six-story project, called Horizon of Oakland Park, will house 311 apartments and 20,700 square feet of retail space. It will rise across four acres located by the southeast corner of Northeast 12th Avenue and Northeast 38th Street, adjacent to North Dixie Highway, in the Broward County city. About 20 percent of units will be priced within 120 percent of the area’s median income. The development — which is expected to cost $133 million total — will include two pickleball courts, a covered playground, and 195 parking spots. Construction is expected to be completed in early 2029. The Boca Raton-based development firm purchased the land for $8.5 million from the City of Oakland Park this month. Horizon of Oakland Park is part of a broader downtown revitalization effort. Next door, NR Investments completed the Sky Building in 2021, a mixed-use development housing a 136-unit rental building and Oakland Park’s new City Hall. The senior construction loan comes about two years after Bank OZK announced its would cap loan originations to under $500 million. For years, it had issued large loans for high-profile projects across South Florida, including the Waldorf Astoria condo tower in Miami and the St. Regis-branded oceanfront condo project in Sunny Isles Beach. Falcone Group, led by Art Falcone, is perhaps best known for being a master developer of the 28-acre Miami Worldcenter. The retail component sold for $210 million this year. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bank OZK provided $85.5M construction loan for Falcone Group's Oakland Park, FL project.
311-unit, six-story Horizon of Oakland Park; $133M total cost; 20% affordable units.
Completion early 2029; land purchased from City of Oakland Park for $8.5M.
stories.summary: Bank OZK supplied an $85.5 million construction loan for Falcone Group's Horizon of Oakland Park, a 311-unit multifamily development in Oakland Park, Florida. The $133 million project will include 20% of units at 120% AMI, amenities including pickleball courts, and 195 parking spots, with completion expected in early 2029. The development is part of a broader downtown revitalization effort.
stories.impact: Strong construction financing availability and lender appetite for Broward County multifamily indicates robust capital markets support for supply growth in South Florida. Public land disposition to private developer at modest $8.5M signals municipality confidence in market absorption; phased completion (early 2029) positions project to capture demand from ongoing Fort Lauderdale/Oakland Park migration and corporate relocations. Affordable component (20% at 120% AMI) may attract institutional investors and low-cost debt.

stories.title: Advanced Real Estate Pays $56 Million for Ontario Multifamily Complex
stories.excerpt: The Mogharebi Group (TMG) arranged the $56,175,000 sale of Casitas Apartment Homes, a 253-unit Inland Empire multifamily community located at 1900 South Campus Ave. in Ontario. EVP Otto Ozen and VP Jordan Pakzad represented the seller, a private Los Angeles owner. The buyer was Orange County-based Advanced Real Estate. The buyer assumed the property’s in-place loan at a below-market interest rate of 3.11%. Built in 1963, the community’s expansive site coverage and single-story design enhance operational efficiency while appealing to a broad renter base, according to TMG. “The Casitas property is a perfect fit for our unique ‘X Fund’,” said Paul Julian, president of Advanced Real Estate. “We were able to trade into this property with the equity from 13 smaller assets that were brought into the Fund (via 721 contributions) in 2023. Those contributing partners now have interest in this institutional-sized asset which will yield much higher returns than their contributed smaller properties.” The post Advanced Real Estate Pays $56 Million for Ontario Multifamily Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Advanced Real Estate acquired 253-unit Casitas Apartments, Ontario for $56.2M.
Buyer assumed in-place 3.11% loan; 1963 vintage single-story design.
Consolidation via 'X Fund'; pooled equity from 13 smaller assets via 721 exchanges.
stories.summary: Advanced Real Estate purchased Casitas Apartment Homes, a 253-unit multifamily property in Ontario, California, for $56.175 million, assuming an existing loan at 3.11%. The 1963-built community features single-story, efficient design. The buyer executed a 1031 exchange strategy, consolidating equity from 13 smaller contributed properties into a larger institutional-grade asset.
stories.impact: Illustrates capital consolidation and 1031-exchange trading into Inland Empire core-plus assets when financing rates remain favorably locked in (3.11% assumption). Low-rate assumption and single-story efficiency appeal may support competitive pricing in Ontario submarket; however, deal is primarily a capital repositioning play rather than a demand signal. Suggests investor preference for scale and operational efficiency over geographic diversification.

stories.title: K. Hovanian Relocates Headquarters to Bell Works Holmdel
stories.excerpt: K. Hovnanian Companies LLC has signed a 72,388-square-foot headquarters relocation at Bell Works, the former Bell Labs research campus located at 101 Crawfords Corner Rd. in Holmdel, NJ. The transaction includes a sublease with iCIMS followed by a direct lease extension with building ownership, Inspired by Somerset Development. “Our team evaluated every scenario, from remaining in place and renewing to expanding and pursuing a relocation, before identifying an exceptional opportunity at Bell Works,” said Peter Ladas, EVP, JLL. “By first structuring a new sublease with iCIMS, followed by a direct lease extension, we were able to secure premium, fully furnished space at favorable economics and greater long-term cost certainty.” Ladas and JLL EVP Scott Stange represented K. Hovnanian. The sublandlord, iCIMS, was represented by Joseph Sarno, Joseph A. Sarno Jr. and Jon Miesel of CBRE. Representing building ownership, Jeff Garibaldi, Lindsey Florio and Tara Keating of NAI James E. Hanson played an instrumental role in facilitating the transaction and securing K. Hovnanian’s long-term commitment. The post K. Hovanian Relocates Headquarters to Bell Works Holmdel appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: K. Hovnanian relocated HQ to 72,388 SF at Bell Works, Holmdel, NJ.
Sublease with iCIMS followed by direct lease extension; premium furnished space.
Former Bell Labs campus; favorable long-term economics and cost certainty.
stories.summary: K. Hovnanian Companies signed a 72,388-square-foot headquarters lease at Bell Works, a redeveloped Bell Labs campus in Holmdel, New Jersey. The transaction was structured as a sublease with iCIMS followed by a direct lease extension with building owner Inspired by Somerset Development, securing premium furnished space at favorable economics.
stories.impact: Major homebuilder HQ relocation to New Jersey (likely from elsewhere in tri-state) signals sustained corporate confidence and operational stability in North Jersey office real estate. Adaptive reuse of Bell Labs campus reduces speculative vacancy risk; however, office consolidation and remote-work trends mean this does not directly correlate to increased multifamily demand in the immediate Holmdel market. No clear secondary effect on residential in-migration or job growth.

stories.title: Creative Design Firm Collins Relocates NYC HQ to 11K SF at 207 Front Street
stories.excerpt: Creative design studio Collins is moving its New York headquarters across the East River. The award-winning firm inked an 11,380-square-foot lease across four floors at Seaport Associates’ 207 Front Street, the tenant’s broker confirmed. The lease covers the entire office portion of the four-story landmarked building, according to Crain’s New York Business, which first reported on the transaction. The five-year deal includes a five-year extension option, and asking rent was around $50 per square foot. Competition for the space was fierce, according to Norman Bobrow & Company’s Jacob Wolkenfeld, who represented Collins alongside Benjamin Schanzer. “We were not the only group competing for it, but won because it was the perfect tenant for the building and the neighborhood to bring more vibrancy,” Wolkenfeld told Commercial Observer. Okada & Company’s Christopher Okada and Parveen Rampersaud represented the landlord. “I believe South Street Seaport is an incredible gem of a location,” Okada told CO. “I think over the next few years it’ll re-emerge as a new go-to destination when the area becomes densely residential.” Collins is currently headquartered in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, at 457 Grand Street. The company has been named Agency of the Year by media brand Ad Age eight times since 2019, according to its website. Collins will relocate its offices — which includes a notable library — to the Lower Manhattan address early next year. The building, part of the neighborhood’s historic South Street Seaport Historic District, was built in 1797. Collins’ deal leaves a 1,300-square-foot open retail space on the ground floor. The building’s ground floor was previously occupied by the now-shuttered chain Big Gay Ice Cream. Collins did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Design firm Collins leased 11,380 SF across four floors at 207 Front Street, Manhattan.
Five-year lease with five-year extension; ~$50/SF asking rent.
South Street Seaport location; competed with other tenants; landlord is Seaport Associates.
stories.summary: Creative design studio Collins signed an 11,380-square-foot lease across four floors at 207 Front Street in Manhattan's South Street Seaport at approximately $50 per square foot. The five-year lease includes a five-year extension option and covers the entire office portion of the four-story landmarked building.
stories.impact: Office leasing momentum in Seaport signals renewed amenity-seeking by creative/professional tenants, but does not directly drive multifamily demand. No employment base expansion or wage-growth signal. Competitive leasing activity supports Seaport revitalization narrative but is noise for multifamily fundamentals; focus on office market dynamics, not residential.

stories.title: Rockland Trust Lends on Income-Restricted Apartments in Malden
stories.excerpt: Rockland Trust recently provided a $10.67-million construction loan to support Asian Community Development Corporation (ACDC)’s new affordable housing development at 213 Main St. in Malden, MA. ACDC’s first development in Malden, the project will create 20 income-restricted apartments. ACDC acquired the property, which formerly housed the Salvation Army, in 202 with funding from the City of Malden. The residential conversion is planned as an all-electric, solar-ready building meeting Enterprise Green Communities and ENERGY STAR standards. A groundbreaking ceremony is set for Monday, Nov. 19. “We are proud to partner with ACDC and support the financing of this important affordable housing development in Malden,” said Kelly Nguyen, SVP commercial banking officer at Rockland Trust. “By helping finance 213 Main St. we are supporting the creation of much-needed housing opportunities while investing in the long-term vitality of Malden and the residents who call it home.” The post Rockland Trust Lends on Income-Restricted Apartments in Malden appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Rockland Trust provided $10.67M construction loan for ACDC's Malden, MA affordable project.
20-unit income-restricted development at 213 Main St.; all-electric, solar-ready.
Adaptive reuse of former Salvation Army building; groundbreaking November 19.
stories.summary: Rockland Trust provided a $10.67 million construction loan to Asian Community Development Corporation (ACDC) for a 20-unit income-restricted affordable housing development at 213 Main Street in Malden, Massachusetts. The all-electric, solar-ready conversion of a former Salvation Army property meets Enterprise Green Communities standards and will serve ACDC's first Malden project.
stories.impact: Demonstrates lender willingness to finance small-scale affordable conversions in suburban Boston (Malden), suggesting stable subsidy/financing stack and municipal support for affordable infill. However, only 20 units provides minimal supply-side market signal. No indication of market-rate rental demand growth or employment in-migration to Malden; primarily a localized policy/subsidy-driven transaction.

stories.title: Fresno Low-Rise Trades to Private Buyer in All-Cash Deal
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s Fresno Investment Sales team of Robin Kane and Brendan Kane arranged the $4-million sale of Las Flores Apartments, a 46-unit low-rise multifamily community at 3420 N. First St. in Fresno. Northmarq represented the seller, a Bay Area investment trust. A private investor purchased the property. “The extensive fire damage at Las Flores created a unique challenge, requiring us to find an all-cash buyer positioned to take on the necessary repairs,” said Robin Kane. Built in 1971, Las Flores Apartments is located along North First Street, one of Fresno’s most prominent residential corridors, offering high visibility and convenient access to major thoroughfares. Robin Kane added, “Fresno’s multifamily market is supported by sustained population growth and increasing household formation, which contribute to renter demand. Even properties requiring substantial rehabilitation can attract investor interest when the opportunity is matched with a buyer prepared to undertake the necessary work.” The post Fresno Low-Rise Trades to Private Buyer in All-Cash Deal appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: All-cash sale of Las Flores Apartments, 46 units, Fresno for $4M.
1971 vintage property; extensive fire damage; private investor buyer.
Fresno market supported by sustained population growth and household formation.
stories.summary: Northmarq arranged the $4 million all-cash sale of Las Flores Apartments, a 46-unit low-rise community in Fresno, from a Bay Area investment trust to a private investor. The 1971-built property required extensive fire damage repairs, necessitating an all-cash buyer. Fresno's market benefits from sustained population growth and household formation.
stories.impact: All-cash transaction for damaged asset signals scarcity of traditional financing for distressed properties and investor capital chasing yield in secondary markets (Fresno). Population growth and household formation tailwinds support fundamental Fresno multifamily demand but are countervailed by high repair costs and investor caution. Limited signal on new development or capital availability for ground-up; suggests investor focus on value-add/fix-and-flip in price-sensitive Central Valley market.

stories.title: RXR Acquires Minority Stake in Silverstein’s 55 Broad Street
stories.excerpt: There’s some new blood in Downtown Manhattan at Silverstein Properties and MetroLoft’s 55 Broad Street. RXR has made a minority investment in the property, which is valued at roughly $500 million, as part of a broader recapitalization that also includes a $305 million senior loan from Wells Fargo. Additionally, Macquarie Capital Principal Finance is also participating in the deal as a capital partner. Newmark arranged the recap with a team consisting of Adam Spies, Adam Doneger, Avery Silverstein, Marcella Fasulo, Doug Harmon and Joshua King. Newmark’s Jordan Roeschlaub, Christopher Kramer and Aaron Golesorkhi negotiated the debt for the deal, which represents the first office-to-resi conversion sale under the 467-m tax abatement, which encourages such conversions, sources said. Silverstein Properties and MetroLoft acquired 55 Broad from Rudin for $180 million in May 2022, CO first reported at the time. The newly completed office-to-residential conversion in Manhattan’s Financial District served as Goldman Sachs’ headquarters until 1983, but has been transformed into a 571-unit mixed-income rental housing property. RXR’s investment was made via RXR Cardinal Venture, its venture with the North Carolina Investment Authority that launched in February. “55 Broad Street brings together many of the attributes we continue to prioritize across our investment platform: a high-quality residential asset, experienced sponsorship, a supply-constrained market and a bespoke capital structure designed to support long-term value creation,” Russ Young, head of investments at RXR, said in a statement. “This transaction also demonstrates the breadth of the RXR capital solutions platform and our ability to invest creatively across the capital structure.” An office-to-resi conversion of the 35-story Lower Manhattan building was completed in 2025, and the property recently achieved 95 percent occupancy, according to RXR. bullets: RXR acquired minority stake in 55 Broad Street, Manhattan; $500M valuation.
Wells Fargo provided $305M senior loan; Macquarie Capital also invested.
First office-to-resi conversion sale under 467-m tax abatement; Silverstein/MetroLoft partners.
stories.summary: RXR made a minority investment in 55 Broad Street, a downtown Manhattan office-to-resi conversion project valued at approximately $500 million, as part of a broader recapitalization that includes a $305 million senior loan from Wells Fargo and capital from Macquarie Capital. The deal represents the first sale under New York's 467-m tax abatement, which incentivizes office-to-residential conversions.
stories.impact: Major capital commitment to office-to-resi conversion signals strong investor and lender appetite for residential conversion plays in Lower Manhattan. 467-m tax abatement de-risks first-mover conversion economics; subsequent deals will reference this transaction. Implications: downtown Manhattan office space repricing downward may accelerate residential conversion pipeline, increasing multifamily supply in FiDi/Seaport submarkets and competing with new-build for capital. Tax incentive sustainability is critical risk—watch for policy changes.

stories.title: Miami-Area Multifamily Project Trades for $54M
stories.excerpt: A 50-year-old apartment complex in the Miami suburb of Kendall has changed hands for $53.5 million, or $200,000 per unit. Residences at 107 Ave., led by Merco Group’s Belinda Meruelo and attorney Felix M. Caceres II of Miami Beach, sold the 267 apartments at 8520 Southwest 107th Avenue to Ralgo Group of Miami, led by Amy L. Gonzalez and Richard A. Gonzalez. The 267-unit complex last traded for $8.5 million in 1995, according to property records. Totaling 283,695 square feet in three stories, the apartment complex was built on the 9.2-acre site in 1972 and 1974. It includes two pools. According to Apartments.com, units rent for $1,750 a month. According to Cushman & Wakefield, the multifamily occupancy rate in Miami’s Kendall submarket was 94.2 percent as of mid-2026. The average monthly rent was $2,306, up 0.6 percent from a year earlier. Recent Kendall transactions include a $65.5 million deal for 10605-10651 Hammocks Boulevard. That 264-unit deal equated to $248,000 per unit. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Residences at 107 Ave. sold 267-unit Kendall complex to Ralgo Group for $53.5M.
$200K/unit; 50-year-old property; last traded $8.5M in 1995.
Kendall occupancy 94.2%, avg. rent $2,306 (up 0.6% YoY); recent comp $248K/unit.
stories.summary: A 267-unit apartment complex in Kendall, Florida (Miami suburb), sold for $53.5 million ($200,000 per unit) to Ralgo Group. The 1972/1974-built property last traded in 1995 for $8.5 million. Kendall submarket shows 94.2% occupancy and average rent of $2,306, up 0.6% year-over-year; recent comparable trades at $248,000 per unit.
stories.impact: Price-per-unit spread ($200K vs. recent $248K comp) suggests valuation variation by property condition/age or buyer profile differences. Kendall's stable 94%+ occupancy and modest rent growth (0.6% YoY) indicate market maturity and limited upside, typical of aging suburban Miami inventory. Miami metro remains attractive for value-add buyers, but this deal does not signal strong demand expansion; suggests investor consolidation of older stock. Monitor Kendall deliveries and competitive new supply—rent growth stalling may constrain cap-rate compression.

stories.title: Irvine Company Signs Nearly 2.5M SF of Office Leases in Q3
stories.excerpt: Irvine Company signed nearly 2.5 million square feet of office leases in the third quarter, led by deals with Taco Bell and medical technology firm Envista and seizing on the overall demand for Orange County, Calif., space compared with its neighbors. The Newport Beach-based private real estate giant completed 182 leases across its national office portfolio from July through September, generating 722,000 square feet of positive net absorption, Commercial Observer can first report. New leases and expansions accounted for more than 1.36 million square feet, while renewals added another 1.06 million square feet. The largest deal was Taco Bell’s 254,000-square-foot lease at Alton HQ in Irvine, marking Orange County’s largest office lease in five years. The fast-food giant plans to relocate its headquarters to the campus in 2028. Envista signed another 117,700-square-foot lease at Irvine Company’s Lakeview Business Center, while transportation technology company Iteris, part of Almaviva Group, committed to 64,000 square feet at Laguna Canyon in Irvine. Other Southern California transactions included a 46,000-square-foot relocation and expansion by Luminys Systems at Bake Technology Park and a 23,000-square-foot renewal by accounting firm Redwitz at Jamboree Center, both in Irvine. “These commitments reflect the value companies continue to place on high-quality workplaces that support their people and their business,” Roger DeWames, president of office properties at Irvine Company, said in a statement. “From Taco Bell’s major lease at Alton HQ to customers renewing and expanding across our portfolio, we’re seeing companies make significant investments in their office space.” Orange County’s office vacancy declined to 12.1 percent in the third quarter from 13.3 percent in the second quarter, while net absorption reached 300,000 square feet, according to CBRE. Average monthly asking rents increased 11 cents to $3 per square foot per month. Mean
bullets: Irvine Company signed 2.5M SF office leases in Q3; 182 leases, 722K SF net absorption.
Taco Bell HQ lease 254K SF at Alton HQ; relocation 2028.
Orange County office strength vs. regional competitors; Envista, Iteris also expanding.
stories.summary: Irvine Company reported 2.5 million square feet of office leases signed in Q3 across 182 deals, generating 722,000 square feet of positive net absorption. The largest was Taco Bell's 254,000-square-foot headquarters lease at Alton HQ in Irvine, slated for 2028 relocation and Orange County's largest office lease in five years. Additional major leases include Envista (117,700 SF) and Iteris (64,000 SF).
stories.impact: Major HQ relocation (Taco Bell) to Irvine signals sustained corporate confidence and talent availability in Orange County, likely attracting in-migration of employees and management. 2028 occupancy will drive near-term housing demand surge in Irvine/OC submarkets; strong office leasing also indicates employer stability and wage growth, supporting multifamily fundamentals. Net absorption of 722K SF shows market tightness—signals supply gap and potential for rents to rise, supporting developer economics. Monitor Irvine multifamily delivery pipeline; window to acquire/build ahead of 2028 Taco Bell influx may be closing.
